title: Terraform configuration
subtitle: Check inputs, create repeated resources and keep secrets out of state.

delta.before: Sensitive output redaction could be mistaken for secret protection.
delta.after: Use ephemeral values and write-only fields, then check the saved state and plan for leaks.

exercises.title: Evaluation Order Visualizer
exercises.description: Step through the checks and see when they run, warn or stop an operation.

exercises.title: State Leak Inspector
exercises.description: See the difference between hiding a password and leaving it out of state.

cost.assumptions: Short-lived resources, no compute, standard parameters, no uploads; gross usage before account credits.

checkpoints.prompt: A password input and root output are marked sensitive. Does this remove their value from state?

rationale.a: Sensitive hides the value in normal output, but it can still be saved in state.
rationale.b: Use an appropriate ephemeral-to-write-only flow to omit the value.

checkpoints.prompt: A check data source reads a managed resource through its ID reference. What do that reference and a false check assertion mean?

choices.a: The reference carries a dependency; the data source reads, and a failed check warns
choices.b: The data source owns deletion; file order controls dependencies and a check always aborts apply

rationale.a: Resources own lifecycle, data sources query, references carry graph edges, and checks are non-blocking assertions.
rationale.b: This confuses ownership, graph ordering and check failure behavior.

checkpoints.prompt: Which design uses unique unordered known service names as stable instance keys?

choices.a: set(string) with for_each over non-sensitive values
choices.b: A tuple with count, because indices never shift after removing an item

rationale.a: A set supplies unique names without positional identity; for_each uses them as keys.
rationale.b: Tuple positions and count indexes can shift; use stable keys when names identify the items.
